title: Quasi-two-dimensional dispersions of Brownian particles with competitive interactions: Dynamical clustering, non-Gaussianity and hydrodynamic correlations
authors: Zihan Tan, Vania Calandrini, Jan K. G. Dhont, Gerhard Nägele
abstract: We conduct a comprehensive dynamical analysis of quasi-two-dimensional (Q2D) dispersions of Brownian particles with competing short-range attractive (SA) and long-range repulsive (LR) interactions using Langevin dynamics (LD) and multiparticle collision dynamics (MPC). As the attractive interaction is strengthened, self-diffusion is significantly suppressed, and clustering gives rise to pronounced subdiffusive behavior. We find that cluster lifetimes are influenced more strongly by attraction strength than by particle concentration. Two dynamical criteria for the transition from non-clustered to clustered phases are identified in terms of the mean cluster lifetime and the relaxation time of local hexagonal order, respectively. Moreover, clustered Q2D-SALR systems exhibit pronounced non-Gaussian dynamics. In particular, the self-van Hove function in the equilibrium-cluster phase displays an approximately exponential form, consistent with an underlying diffusing-diffusivity mechanism. Importantly, MPC simulations reveal the critical role of hydrodynamic interactions (HIs) in collective dynamics. We observe that the anomalously enhanced large-scale collective diffusion characteristic of hydrodynamically interacting Q2D systems is qualitatively preserved in Q2D-SALR dispersions. However, this enhancement suppresses the intermediate-range-order peak in the hydrodynamic function compared to its three-dimensional counterpart. Furthermore, by analyzing the time-dependent evolution of hydrodynamic function and the sound mode in hydrodynamic correlations, we find that clustering in Q2D-SALR systems leads to an earlier onset of HIs than in Q2D hard-sphere reference systems, implying HIs become relevant already on inertial timescales.
summary: This work provides a comprehensive dynamical analysis of colloidal particles with competing attractions in 2D, revealing how attractive interactions drive clustering and subdiffusion. By combining advanced simulations (MPC) with diagnostics like non-Gaussian parameters and hydrodynamic functions, the authors map out phase transitions governed by cluster lifetimes and show that collective hydrodynamics are significantly modified by these transient clusters.
main_problem: The study investigates how competing short-range attractive (SA) and long-range repulsive (LR) interactions affect the collective dynamics, clustering behavior, and hydrodynamic correlations of Brownian particles confined to a quasi-two-dimensional plane.
main_result: Clustering significantly suppresses self-diffusion and leads to pronounced subdiffusive behavior; furthermore, the analysis reveals that hydrodynamic interactions become relevant on inertial timescales due to the presence of attractive interactions.
method: The research employs advanced simulation techniques, including Langevin Dynamics (LD) and Multiparticle Collision Dynamics (MPC), alongside theoretical diagnostics like non-Gaussian parameters and time-dependent correlation functions.
model_or_system: The system is a Q2D dispersion of identical spherical Brownian particles interacting via a pair potential combining SA and LR components. The analysis spans various dynamic phases, including Dispersed Fluid, Equilibrium Clusters, Random Percolation, and Cluster Percolation.
key_observables: Self-diffusion coefficient, non-Gaussian parameters ($\alpha_n$, $\gamma^{(d=2)}$), cluster lifetime ($	au_b$), relaxation time of local hexagonal order ($	au_6$), and the hydrodynamic function $H(q)$.
important_parameters: Area fraction ($\phi_{2D}$), effective temperature ($T^*$), attraction strength, and wavevector ($q$).
main_assumptions: The use of MPC to resolve fluctuating hydrodynamics is key; approximations are made regarding collision time steps in the simulation setup.
figures_summary: Figures summarize phase diagrams ($\phi_{2D} - T^*/T_c$), MSD vs. time showing subdiffusion, and time-evolution plots of correlation functions ($B(t)$, $g_6(t)$) to distinguish fluid from clustered states.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the system by first characterizing local structure (bond correlations, hexagonal order), then quantifying particle dynamics via non-Gaussianity, and finally examining collective transport through hydrodynamic function analysis in different phase regimes.
why_interesting: While focused on classical colloidal systems, the detailed mathematical framework for analyzing dynamic heterogeneity using generalized non-Gaussian parameters ($\gamma^{(d=2)}$) and the coupling of structural arrest to long-range hydrodynamic correlations are highly relevant methodologies applicable to understanding complex many-body quantum dynamics in confined geometries.
